method.description: The operation to perform. Use view to inspect current policies, update to modify existing policies, archive to retire policies, create to add new policies, create_domain to add a routing domain, update_domain to improve a domain description, and exit when reflection is complete.

reason.description: Optional short explanation of the operation. Use it with exit to say why reflection is stopping (e.g. no preferences found, all changes complete).

request.description: A list of requests for the selected operation. Multiple policies may be handled in one operation. For exit, this must be an empty array.

id.description: The policy identifier. For view, update, and archive this identifies the existing policy. For create, this is the new unique policy identifier (snake_case). Ids are immutable once created — to supersede a policy under a new id, create the new policy with a `replaces` entry naming the old id.

title.description: A concise human-readable name for the preference.

body.description: The durable preference expressed as a concise, reusable imperative instruction. It must describe general decision intent rather than implementation details.

description.description: For create_domain and update_domain: concise description of the routing context.

priority.description: How strongly the preference defines the user's decision style (its importance). Set by judgment, not by counting evidence: 85-95 core identity, 70-85 strong, 50-70 situational, 30-50 weak/experimental. Change only when the preference's importance is reclassified.

applies_to.description: Domains where this preference applies. Use only domains supplied by the system. Changes to applicability require strong evidence.

primary_domain.description: The single domain most specifically targeted by the preference. Use only a supplied domain.

exceptions.description: IDs of other preferences that provide contextual exceptions or overrides. These are informational relationships, not executable logic.

related.description: IDs of preferences with similar or overlapping decision intent. This is a non-hierarchical relationship used for grouping and deduplication.

replaces.description: Create only: IDs of existing policies this new policy supersedes. The engine rewires references to the new id and archives the replaced policies automatically. Optional.

positive_observations.description: Observation IDs (in "session_id:turn_index" form, matching the [N] markers in the transcript) that provide positive evidence for this preference.

negative_observations.description: Observation IDs (in "session_id:turn_index" form) that provide negative or contradictory evidence for this preference.

evidence.description: New evidence observations associated with the policy. Evidence counts and confidence are derived by the policy engine — never set them yourself.
